title: One kindness
tomorrow: Paul says examine yourselves. he also says he won't. which?

cards: At some memorials, people line up at a microphone to tell stories. In Acts, at Joppa, nobody gives a speech at all. A disciple named Tabitha, also called Dorcas, has died, and her friends send for Peter.
When he comes into the upper room, the widows stand around him weeping, “shewing the coats and garments which Dorcas made, while she was with them.” Why coats? Why not a eulogy?

teach.b: Acts gives her one line of description: “this woman was full of good works and almsdeeds which she did.” Then, instead of explaining, it shows.
A coat, then another, held up one at a time. That's the solve. Each garment was made for somebody in particular, and each widow is holding hers.
Dorcas's goodness wasn't a mood spread thin over everyone. It came one coat at a time, each with a name on it. Peter sends everyone out, kneels and prays, and she opens her eyes.
But before the miracle, the story lingers on the pile of clothes. Jesus sets the bar low on purpose.

teach.h: A CUP OF COLD WATER ONLY.
teach.b: In Matthew, whoever gives “a cup of cold water only” to one of his little ones won't lose the reward. A cup of water. Only.
And Ephesians puts it plainly: “be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another.”
Thérèse of Lisieux, from earlier this year, called her path the little way and wrote about small, hidden kindnesses in an ordinary day.
So one kindness means one deliberate act, chosen on purpose, for one person. Something to tell a friend tonight: Acts remembers Dorcas with a pile of coats, not a speech.

how: Some Christians choose one deliberate kindness each day, often small and unseen, as a way of following Jesus, and some church groups still sew and knit clothing for people in need.

o: one deliberate act of kindness for one person
a single good deed that makes up for a sin
being polite to strangers as a daily rule

games.q: the coats at Joppa — tap the pairs.
p: made coats and garments for the widows

s: Acts remembers Dorcas with a long speech about her
the widows showed Peter the coats she made.
kindness only counts if it's a big gesture
a cup of cold water only, Jesus says.
Tabitha and Dorcas are the same woman

games.q: you want to be kinder this month. which plan fits the Dorcas story?
o: be extra nice to everyone you meet, all the time.
one specific kindness a day, for one named person.
save it all up for one big charity event at month's end.
games.why: Dorcas's goodness came one coat at a time, each for somebody in particular. the widows could each hold up theirs.

practice: Pick up your phone and bring one person to mind who could use something small today. Send them one specific kindness, not a general hello: thanks for something exact, an offer of one concrete thing, a memory they'd smile at.
If you pray, hold their name for a moment as it sends.
